policy: Use the saved verbal brand style below for look and feel. Library inspiration pixels are not attached and must not be requested again during campaign planning or generation. Observations and draft guidance are suggestions, not mandatory requirements or product proof. Adapt the setting to this brief and exact product; do not mechanically reproduce a reference bedroom. Do not claim to have inspected missing pixels. Exact SKU photos, identity assets, current artwork and repair masks remain separate visual evidence.

preferences.text: Proposal, not approved guidance: explore contemporary, tactile domestic settings where architecture, circulation and light make room for pausing, connecting and participating again. Treat the draft guide and reference interiors as inspiration, not specifications.

The draft proposes warm neutrals with selected deeper or natural tones and tactile surfaces. These are exploratory relationships, not approved swatches, material specifications or a requirement to make every scene beige.

Official imagery shows a red symbol and uppercase DUROFLEX; treat this as observed identity, not a complete production specification. Confirm approved logo, lockup and typography rather than reconstructing them from draft slides.
Draft proposal: favor believable domestic actions and relaxed contact over presenter-like posing. Casting, wardrobe and gestures remain creative choices, not approved mandatory rules.
The official site shows varied category and promotional treatments. These are dated examples of current practice, not a permanent visual system or a requirement to imitate sale styling.

observations.title: Let architecture and circulation create calm
observations.text: Proposed application: plan the entrance, openings, product footprint, storage, activity zone and passage before choosing décor. The inspected R20 reference integrates a workstation and mirror with a bedroom; V018 relates low furniture to broad openings, wall planes and recessed storage. Borrow legible domestic organisation rather than copying reference furniture. Keep bedside access and seating approaches usable, with tables outside verified extension paths. Reserve genuine wall and floor space without making the product tiny. Spatial clarity communicates an impression of ease, not demonstrated stress reduction.

observations.title: Material and colour relationships matter more than beige minimalism
observations.text: The draft proposes bone, sand, taupe and stone alongside sage, olive, clay, wine, midnight blue and soft sky. Inspected R20 contrasts sage walls, darker timber outlines and pale textiles; R36 layers timber-looking planes, neutral bedding and directional light. V018 adds texture and greenery rather than colourlessness. These support tonal separation and tactile variety, not approved swatches or authenticated material composition. Product colour must remain unchanged; room surfaces should support it rather than force every category into one neutral palette.

observations.title: Make light explain the room and camera explain use
observations.text: Proposed production approach: establish one credible principal light source, supported by believable practical lamps. R36 visibly connects left glazing to wall and floor shadows. Use frontal framing for silhouette, three-quarter views for depth and circulation, and close views for contact and construction. Preserve SKU colour, fabric grain and floor contact rather than adding a warm cast everywhere. The draft names morning, quiet-day and evening modes, but the indexed review finds repeated daylight examples under evening headings; intended time therefore needs separate lighting references, not assumption from captions.

observations.title: Direct supported actions, natural contact and relaxed wardrobe
observations.text: The draft favours reading, turning, reclining, stretching and companionship over presenter poses or forced smiles. Proposed direction: check pelvis, back, head, feet, hands, cushion compression, occlusion and garment tension together. Use relaxed, matte, tactile homewear with enough tonal contrast to reveal contact; the draft suggests linen, washed cotton, jersey and muted colours. Indian relevance is a casting intention, not something to infer from faces. The indexed character appendix includes fashion-like poses and lustrous clothing that do not consistently match these instructions; its locked caption remains draft.

observations.title: Six room families provide a flexible—not mandatory—spatial menu
observations.text: Derived proposals: (1) Compact connected home—integrate sleep, storage and a modest work/activity zone. (2) Garden-threshold reset—use framed greenery, low horizons and an accessible outdoor edge. (3) Filtered-light contemporary room—borrow screen depth without transplanting a complete themed interior. (4) Warm social lounge—make conversation and seating extension legible. (5) Sheltered reading/recovery corner—provide reachable light, controls and a clear approach. (6) Colour-led bedroom—use one restrained wall/recess tone around the unchanged SKU. These are advisory translations from the indexed references, not six approved sets; avoid resort spectacle, obstructive benches and accumulated ornament.

observations.title: Mattresses: one domestic foundation, distinct Airboost and Duropedic treatments
observations.text: Proposed mattress world: a usable bedroom with opening-led daylight, bedside storage and enough exposed edge, quilting and branding to identify the variant. Airboost can use restrained blue-white freshness and a separately verified technical view—not a blue cast, floating mattress or invented cutaway. Duropedic can express human trust through warm domestic architecture and supported everyday rest—not medical theatre, pain grimaces or anatomical glows. The indexed official selection includes ornate bedroom settings; retain product clarity without inheriting chandeliers or hotel staging. Turning, reading and waking are narrative actions, not airflow or orthopedic proof.

observations.title: Sofas and motion: social release with accurate mechanics
observations.text: Proposed direction: build a connected conversation or entertainment zone rather than a matching showroom set. Let the exact upholstery colour lead against quieter architecture; use natural, independent postures for shared reading or conversation. Develop daylight and practical-lit evening versions separately. For motion products, pair the closed silhouette with a verified extended configuration and supported use, keeping tables and people clear of the mechanism. Ports, motors and reclining geometry must come from the selected model, not another sofa or collection-wide copy. This interprets the draft's Evening Exhale mood without making every lounge dark.

observations.title: Recliners: a personal pause within an accessible home
observations.text: Proposed recliner setting: a sheltered reading corner with reachable lighting, a usable approach and visible support for arms, back and lower legs. Selectively deeper wall tones can frame the chair without hiding upholstery or controls. The indexed study contrasts transferable domestic settings with floral coastal arches; borrow enclosure and chair visibility, not resort scenery. Show only the selected chair's documented positions and operation. Category placement or a resting pose cannot establish rocking, rotation, powered adjustment, therapeutic benefit or outdoor suitability.

observations.title: Beds and smart sleep: distinguish architectural form from function
observations.text: Proposed approach: decide whether the bed frame, mattress or complete combination is the hero. Give upholstered beds readable headboard shape, fabric and room access; demonstrate storage separately where documented. For smart sleep, distinguish mattress firmness adjustment from bed articulation, and show only a verified compatible combination. Reading, preparing for bed or getting up provides domestic context. Bedding that conceals articulation cannot demonstrate adjustment. The indexed sage-and-clay bedroom treatment is one useful precedent, not a universal bed palette or proof of the product labels' portfolio status.

observations.title: Pillows and accessories: close, specific contact rather than generic softness
observations.text: Proposed Micro Restoration treatment: intimate bedside context, touch and clearly visible surface detail. Match head contact, adjustment or seated use to the actual pillow form; preserve contour, edging and pattern. For toppers, protectors and comforters, make the selected item identifiable rather than allowing styling to hide it. The indexed website examples mix dark graphics, blue use scenes and yellow packaging, so no single accessory palette is established. Appearance and poses cannot substantiate loft, fibre composition, cooling, alignment or health outcomes.

observations.title: Massagers: explain technology through correct domestic use
observations.text: Proposed recovery world: a warm, functional corner with clear device access, grounded contact and understandable controls—neither spa spectacle nor clinic. The draft includes a domestic foot-device precedent, whereas the indexed official visuals commonly isolate devices on dark fields. Supplement form recognition with documented seated use, keeping open and closed configurations distinct. Do not invent body contact, heat glows, treatment durations or device capabilities. Clinical and healing language on W11 is current marketing copy, not independent substantiation or permission to depict medical outcomes.
